title: MrMap Celery task performance
description: Celery task-performance series of #1391 (epic #1387 V2): who occupies the workers, which classes are slow, and the drill-down from a slow class to one attempt. Published by system.tasks.publish_task_performance while MRMAP_TASK_PERFORMANCE_EXPORT=on; the record contract and the operator runbook are in docs/source/development/celery-task-performance.rst.

panels.title: Fleet occupancy (worker slot seconds per window)
panels.description: What fraction of the worker pool was busy. One record per window (MRMAP_TASK_PERFORMANCE_EXPORT_WINDOW_MINUTES); an empty bucket means beat did not fire, not that nothing ran - see the windows panel. docs/source/development/celery-task-performance.rst (#1391).

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=fleet" | extract `slot_seconds=<slot_seconds> ` | stats by (_time:5m) sum(slot_seconds) as slot_seconds

panels.title: Windows emitted (fire coverage)
panels.description: Coverage of the series itself: seconds of window actually published. A gap here is a missing beat fire, and any gap in the other panels means this one first.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=fleet" | extract `window_seconds=<window_seconds> ` | stats by (_time:5m) sum(window_seconds) as window_seconds

panels.title: Task class occupancy (slot seconds)
panels.description: Who occupies the workers: worker slot seconds per task class per window. The class is the module of the task name under the bounded class rule of #1326, so the cardinality stays bounded.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=class_bucket" | extract `task_class=<task_class> ` | extract `slot_seconds=<slot_seconds> ` | stats by (task_class, _time:5m) sum(slot_seconds) as slot_seconds | sort by (slot_seconds desc)

panels.title: Task class occupancy (interval total)
panels.description: The same series ranked over the whole interval - the row an operator clicks into.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=class_bucket" | extract `task_class=<task_class> ` | extract `slot_seconds=<slot_seconds> ` | stats by (task_class) sum(slot_seconds) as slot_seconds | sort by (slot_seconds desc)

panels.title: Slow classes (95th percentile of a run)
panels.description: Slow-task operator drill-down entry: the wall time of the 95th percentile of a single run, highest window of the interval. Absent means nothing was measured, not fast - #1330 keeps the two apart.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=class_bucket" | extract `task_class=<task_class> ` | extract `active_p95=<active_p95> ` | stats by (task_class) max(active_p95) as active_p95 | sort by (active_p95 desc)

panels.title: Attempts still open, by class (running vs past the grace)
panels.description: The standing state of the attempt table, read off the coverage records of the last fire: open_running is an attempt the fleet may still be executing (expected, and a genuinely long-running task keeps showing here), open_abandoned is an attempt older than the abandon grace whose worker never reported an end - the crash residue. The two are never added together: a long task must not read as crashed workers. Newest fire per class, never an aggregate: these records are a gauge read per fire, so max() over the interval would show the worst fire of the window after a deployment recovered from its crash, and sum() would count one residue once per fire.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=class_coverage" | extract `task_class=<task_class> ` | extract `open_running=<open_running> ` | extract `open_abandoned=<open_abandoned> ` | extract `open_total=<open_total> ` | fields _time, task_class, open_running, open_abandoned, open_total | sort by (_time) desc | limit 40

panels.title: Failed, retried and revoked attempts (per window)
panels.description: The outcomes of the window, from the fleet record: the issue asks for failures and retries to be visible without a broker export, and they are the first thing to compare against a class which suddenly occupies more of the workers - a retry burns the slot again. Plotted per window rather than per interval, because a retry storm is a moment, not a total. An absent line is an unmeasured count of #1330, not a zero.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=fleet" | extract `failed=<failed> ` | stats by (_time:5m) sum(failed) as failed
"Celery task performance" "event=fleet" | extract `retried=<retried> ` | stats by (_time:5m) sum(retried) as retried
"Celery task performance" "event=fleet" | extract `revoked=<revoked> ` | stats by (_time:5m) sum(revoked) as revoked

panels.title: Queue wait beside wall time (95th percentile)
panels.description: The two durations of #1330, on one plot and deliberately never added: a task is slow either because it waited for a worker or because it ran long, and the two have different fixes - more workers versus a smaller task. wait_p95 is only a number where a publish timestamp made it measurable; the wait_coverage of the fleet record says how much of the window had one.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=fleet" | extract `wait_p95=<wait_p95> ` | stats by (_time:5m) max(wait_p95) as wait_p95
"Celery task performance" "event=fleet" | extract `active_p95=<active_p95> ` | stats by (_time:5m) max(active_p95) as active_p95

panels.title: Queues (executions and occupancy)
panels.description: Executions and worker slot seconds per queue, without a broker export.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=class_bucket" | extract `queue=<queue> ` | extract `executions=<executions> ` | extract `slot_seconds=<slot_seconds> ` | stats by (queue) sum(executions) as executions, sum(slot_seconds) as slot_seconds | sort by (executions desc)

panels.title: Periodic tasks behind the samples
panels.description: Which beat rows the sampled attempts came from; the empty name is a task called directly. Epic #1324: a row which stops firing shows up as its absence here.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=class_sample" | extract `periodic_name=<periodic_name> ` | stats by (periodic_name) count() as samples

panels.title: Drill-down samples of the heaviest classes
panels.description: The operator's path from a slow class to one attempt: task_id is the key of the CeleryTaskAttempt of #1330. Capped on purpose (MRMAP_TASK_PERFORMANCE_EXPORT_DRILLDOWN_CLASSES x MRMAP_TASK_PERFORMANCE_EXPORT_SAMPLES_PER_CLASS).

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=class_sample" | extract `task_class=<task_class> ` | extract `task_id=<task_id> ` | extract `outcome=<outcome> ` | extract `active_seconds=<active_seconds> ` | extract `wait_seconds=<wait_seconds> ` | fields _time, task_class, task_id, outcome, active_seconds, wait_seconds | sort by (_time) desc

panels.title: Coverage of the deployment (crash residue right now)
panels.description: The series reports its own gaps: attempts still open without an end, split by whether they may still be running or are past the abandon grace. A deployment whose workers died mid-task shows open_abandoned > 0 even though it publishes no executions. Read the residue row before trusting any number beside it. Newest fire, never an aggregate: this is the standing state of the table read at every fire, so max() over the interval answers how bad the worst fire of the window was - and keeps showing a crash the deployment has since recovered from.

targets.expr: "Celery task performance" "event=coverage" | extract `open_running=<open_running> ` | extract `open_abandoned=<open_abandoned> ` | extract `open_total=<open_total> ` | fields _time, open_running, open_abandoned, open_total | sort by (_time) desc | limit 1
